decisions.reason: Correct: the accepted record asks for the real command validation and names push-check extended for a push, and the plan departs from both. The plan will state the departure, make Increment A ask the owner for a dated clarification note or a new record, and block B until that is settled; I cannot edit the accepted record.

Correct: whether a ref exists on the remote cannot be known from local data. target_refs will list only the refs the push asks to update or delete, with no create-versus-update claim, and the equality test compares requests, not outcomes.
Correct: a reflog is local and forgeable. The fact is renamed to say it only looks written by git, and the spec text must tell the engine to treat it as untrusted evidence.

Correct: the policy says a security review runs only when the owner asks, and approval of a plan is not that. Increment F will stop and ask at that point, use the installed security-review module, and end in a commit that records the pass or the owner declining.

Correct: superseding only item 6 leaves items 1 and 2 in conflict, and a clarification note cannot override an accepted decision. The plan will require a new record, accepted by the owner, that narrows items 1, 2 and 6 for a push and says why the restricted parser is safe; the note option is dropped.

Correct: a list of destination names loses the source, the delete and the force of each refspec. The facts will be separate flat lists for updates as source and destination pairs, deletes, and forced destinations, and the real-push tests must include an empty-source delete and two sources with one destination.

Correct: the endpoint of a push is the push URL, not the fetch URL. The plan will take the scheme and the credential flag from the effective push URL that git reports after pushurl and rewrite rules, never print it, and test url and pushurl that differ.

Correct: follow-tags and mirror pushes depend on what the remote holds, which local data cannot show. The grammar will refuse them, and the same settings in configuration, with a named code, instead of reporting a partial target list; the completion criterion and tests follow.

Correct: git pushes to every configured push URL, so one scheme and one flag cannot describe it. A remote with more than one effective push endpoint will be refused with a named code and a test; per-endpoint facts are deferred.
